The site pipeline and report

Source: vignettes/reporting.Rmd
reporting.Rmd
library(lifr)
demo <- system.file("extdata", "demo", package = "lifr")

One call

process_site() chains the pipeline: import, an optional edit plan, corrections, QA summary, site charts, and the report.

out  <- tempfile("site")
plan <- data.frame(boring = c("*", "LIF-02"), action = c("delete", "keep"),
                   top = c(0, 6), bottom = c(1, 28))

site <- process_site(
  demo,
  edits          = plan,                       # or a path to edits.csv
  corrections    = list(hp = list(water_table = 6)),
  output_dir     = out,
  site_name      = "Demo site",
  report_formats = c("html", "md"),
  quiet          = TRUE)
site
#> <lif_site> Demo site
#>   12 boring(s), 1489 sample(s), 3 edit(s), 4 chart(s)
#>   report(s): /tmp/RtmpC2VHvc/site206855ec0ff9/demo_site_report.html, /tmp/RtmpC2VHvc/site206855ec0ff9/demo_site_report.md

The returned lif_site object holds everything the report was built from:

names(site)
#> [1] "data"      "raw_data"  "site_name" "log"       "summary"   "edits"    
#> [7] "charts"    "reports"   "meta"
site$log
#>      step               action
#> 1  import         lif_import()
#> 2   edits    lif_apply_edits()
#> 3 correct      hp_correction()
#> 4  charts export_site_charts()
#>                                                                                                                                     detail
#> 1                                                                                        /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/lifr/extdata/demo
#> 2                                                                                                                            2 edit row(s)
#> 3                                                                                                                            water_table=6
#> 4 demo_site_chart_max_response.png, demo_site_chart_peak_by_boring.png, demo_site_chart_hp_histogram.png, demo_site_chart_ec_histogram.png
#>   n_rows n_borings
#> 1   1489        12
#> 2   1489        12
#> 3   1489        12
#> 4   1489        12
head(site$edits)
#>                   timestamp              fn boring top bottom value
#> 1 2026-09-04 20:43:13 +0000 lif_editor_bulk   <NA>   0      1     0
#> 2 2026-09-04 20:43:13 +0000        lif_keep LIF-02   6     28     0
#> 3 2026-09-04 20:43:13 +0000   hp_correction   <NA>  NA     NA    NA
#>   n_rows_changed                                           notes
#> 1             48                                            <NA>
#> 2             55 kept 6-28 ft; zeroed rows outside these windows
#> 3           1489                   gradient=0.433; water_table=6
basename(unlist(site$reports))
#> [1] "demo_site_report.html" "demo_site_report.md"

site$data is the processed frame (classed, with its edit history) and site$raw_data is the frame exactly as imported, so you can keep working with either.

Arguments worth knowing

Argument What it does
edits A CSV path or data frame for lif_apply_edits(). See vignette("editing").
corrections list(zero_shallow = 1) zeroes the top foot; zero_below = 0.5 zeroes readings under 0.5 %RE; hp = TRUE or hp = list(water_table = 6, gradient = 0.433) runs hp_correction(). Applied in that order, after the edits.
crs The projected EPSG code of the coordinates. When given, the report adds a boring map over USGS aerial imagery (needs network access; degrades to a note offline).
response_thresholds The Summary tab lists borings whose peak exceeds each value (default 1, 10, 50 %RE).
report_formats Any of "html", "md", "pdf".
date_suffix Appends _YYMMDD to every output name so successive runs sit side by side.
prefix Filename prefix; default is a slug of site_name.

What gets written 

list.files(out)
#> [1] "demo_site_chart_ec_histogram.png"   "demo_site_chart_ec.png"            
#> [3] "demo_site_chart_hp_histogram.png"   "demo_site_chart_hp.png"            
#> [5] "demo_site_chart_max_response.png"   "demo_site_chart_peak_by_boring.png"
#> [7] "demo_site_map_response.png"         "demo_site_report.html"             
#> [9] "demo_site_report.md"
  • <prefix>_report.html: the self-contained HTML report.
  • <prefix>_report.md plus <prefix>_map_*.png and <prefix>_chart_*.png sidecars: the Markdown report. Keep them together when moving it.
  • <prefix>_chart_*.png: the site charts from export_site_charts().
  • With "pdf": <prefix>_report.pdf (rendered from the Markdown through pandoc and LaTeX) and <prefix>_logs.pdf, one page per boring, drawn by R’s own PDF device so it needs no LaTeX.

The HTML report

Open the HTML file in any browser. It needs no server and no internet connection; the figures are embedded and the tables sort when you click a heading. Printing lays every tab out as its own section.

Summary. Stat tiles (borings, samples, depth range, channels, edits), the boring maps, the %RE disclosure, a table of every boring’s peak response and the depth it occurred at, and one table per screening threshold listing the borings above it.

Data & QA. A per-boring inventory (samples, top and bottom depth, native sampling interval, channels present), the summary statistics from summarize_lif() with units, the site charts, and a definitions footnote.

Processing history. The chronological record: what was imported, the complete edit log, the corrections, and the pipeline steps with row and boring counts. This is the audit trail a reviewer reads to answer “what did you do to the data?”

Boring logs. One section per boring showing the input log beside the edited log with the zeroed depth windows shaded red; whole-log operations without a window are named beneath the panel. A “changed borings only” filter and a navigation strip make a 40-boring site quick to scan, and each changed boring carries a badge naming its edited windows.

html <- readLines(site$reports$html, warn = FALSE)
grep("data-tab=", html, value = TRUE)[1:4]

Re-rendering without re-importing

site_report() renders any subset of formats from the object:

site_report(site, formats = "md", output_dir = out, file_prefix = "demo_again",
            quiet = TRUE)

That is the way to add a PDF after the fact, or to render into a different folder.

The PDF toolchain

The main PDF is produced by rmarkdown from the Markdown report, which needs pandoc (bundled with RStudio) and a LaTeX distribution with xelatex. The easiest way to get one:

install.packages("tinytex")
tinytex::install_tinytex()

When either piece is missing, process_site() still writes the other formats and the logs PDF, and says so in a warning.

Reproducibility

Keep the survey folder, the edits CSV, and the process_site() call in a script. Re-running it reproduces every figure and table, and the edit log in the report records the exact windows applied. With date_suffix = TRUE, successive runs are kept side by side instead of overwriting each other.
